summary: Experimental western larch fire tower completed March 1934 in Shawnee National Forest; listed as removed, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Experimental tower of western larch timbers, completed March 1934; a NARA caption calls it one of the first of eight built of western larch
facts.status_note: Listed as removed; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows it as 'Tower Gone'. No removal date in the sources read.
facts.agency: Shawnee National Forest, Delta Ranger District

events.note: Completed March 1934 as an experimental tower of western larch timbers; the NARA caption says it was one of the first of eight built of western larch.
NARA photograph dated June 1941 shows the tower.
A 1942 description calls it a Forest Service fire tower about three miles northwest of Elco.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Central Illinois list and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list use 'Bass Hill'; the NARA caption and the Wikidata alias use 'Base Hill'. The story uses Bass Hill and mentions the variant.

photos.credit: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration, via Wikimedia Commons
photos.license: NARA cooperation upload; Commons says NARA images are public domain or freely licensed (the file's own tag was not checked)
photos.caption: Base Hill Lookout tower, one of the first of eight built of western larch (NARA caption).

notes_for_editor: No source gives a removal date, so no removal event is recorded. No staffing, fire or access facts were found, so those keys are omitted. The site is not described today by any source read. The Commons photo URL is the file page; the direct image URL was not resolved. The 1942 description is quoted through the Central Illinois page.
